_comment: Behavior cases are scoped to code generation ("Do not download or install
anything") because the real vendoring step downloads a binary from GitHub,
which hangs on a runner with no egress. They lean on `logs_contain` rather
than a judged expectation wherever the thing being checked is a literal:
it is instant and free where a judge costs a second agent call.
None of these prompts name the skill. An earlier version of these tests did
("Use the local-ai-app-integration skill"), which made them useless as
routing cases -- and every case here is now also a routing case.

expected_matches.prompt: My Electron app calls the OpenAI chat completions endpoint. I want to ship an offline mode that bundles the inference engine into the installer so it still works with no internet.
My Python desktop tool talks to the Anthropic Messages API today. Give it a mode where the model runs on the customer's own PC so their data never leaves the machine.
Can you vendor an inference binary into my app and repoint my existing HTTP client at it instead of the Ollama server I'm hitting now?
I want my app to compute embeddings on the end user's hardware rather than calling a hosted embeddings API. How do I wire that up?

expected_matches.note: The launcher is the core artifact: a random API key, a dynamically bound port, and lemond spawned as a subprocess.
expected_matches.prompt: Help me add local AI to this Python app so it replaces the OpenAI API with a local backend. Do not download or install anything, just write the launcher module.
should_not: Hardcode a fixed port instead of binding one dynamically

expected_matches.note: Readiness has two documented failure modes: scraping stdout, and pre-loading the model at startup.
expected_matches.prompt: Write a health-check helper for this Python app that waits until the local inference server is ready to serve. Do not download or install anything, just write the code.
should_not: Read or parse the local server's stdout or stderr to detect readiness
Call POST /api/v1/load to pre-load the model at startup

expected_matches.note: The 120-second timeout is the one the skill exists to get right: first-token latency on a cold local model blows past the OpenAI SDK default.
expected_matches.prompt: Update main.py to point the OpenAI client at a local inference server running on this machine. Do not download or install anything, just edit the file.
Edit main.py so the app starts in local mode without an OPENAI_API_KEY. Do not download or install anything, just edit the file.
should: Remove or bypass the API-key guard so the app starts in local mode without requiring OPENAI_API_KEY to be set

expected_no_matches.note: Touches an app's OpenAI integration, but wants it to stay in the cloud.
expected_no_matches.prompt: Add rate limiting and retry-with-backoff to the OpenAI API calls in my Express server.

expected_no_matches.note: Bundling and shipping an app, with no local inference anywhere in it.
expected_no_matches.prompt: Package my Python app as a standalone Windows installer with PyInstaller so users don't need Python.
